title: LLM-HD: Layout Language Model for Hotspot Detection with GDS Semantic Encoding
problem: Layout hotspot detection approaches lose foreground information (metal polygons) and accumulate irrelevant background data when converting binary GDSII files to images, degrading detection quality and wasting computational resources. This degradation is compounded by rapid technology node downscaling and increasingly complex designs.
motivation: Fast and accurate layout hotspot detection is essential for meeting time-to-market constraints in modern semiconductor design under advanced technology nodes.
method: Instead of converting chip layouts to images (which loses important details), this method reads the raw GDSII file—a binary format that describes chip layouts—directly as a semantic representation (a structured description of how design elements relate). A pre-trained language model then processes this as a sequence, like analyzing text. This preserves all the metal polygon details and eliminates the noise from image conversion.
key_novelty: For the first time, layout hotspots are detected by processing the hierarchical chip layout format directly as semantic sequences for language models, rather than converting it to images for vision models.
contributions: Novel layout hotspot detection paradigm operating directly on binary GDS files without image conversion
Hierarchical GDS semantic representation scheme that preserves layout structure and foreground information
Application of pre-trained NLP models to semiconductor layout hotspot detection
Improved accuracy and efficiency over SOTA on ICCAD2012 (metal layer) and ICCAD2020 (via layer) benchmarks

metrics.accuracy: improved over SOTA on ICCAD2012 metal layer and ICCAD2020 via layer benchmarks
metrics.efficiency: improved computational efficiency compared to image-based approaches
